I couldn't open any of the cited files — the working directory has no repo and file tools aren't available in this session — so this is a review of the document's structure and internal logic, not a verification of its evidence.

## Headline: this is two documents wearing one hat, and neither is an implementation plan

It's an audit-findings memo plus a decision log. Against the plan standard for this repo it has: no goal/architecture/tech-stack header, no global constraints, no file-structure map, no tasks, no interfaces block, no test-first steps, no commands with expected output, no commits. A fresh implementer handed this cannot start work on any line of it.

Worse, the status header and the body disagree about what's still live:

- Header: "P0 SHIPPED (PR #320 merged 28-Jul)." Body: P0 still reads as nine imperative future-tense fixes.
- Header: "P1 DECIDED (ADR 0095)." Body: P1 still presents options (a)/(b)/(c) as an open owner call.
- Header: "ADR 0097 skill-assay rename (executes LAST, own PR)... rename CONFIRMED by owner 29-Jul." Body P2b: "Decide: rename plugin vs README disambiguation."

A reader can't tell which sections are history and which are work. Split it: one `docs/decisions/`-style status record (what shipped, what's decided, with PR/ADR ids), and one plan per shippable batch containing actual tasks. Right now the header is doing the work the body should have been rewritten to reflect.

## The sharpest problem is the one the document itself diagnoses

Your verdict paragraph says 100% of open work and the last 10 days of merges went to the measuring apparatus while lever 1 produced nothing. Then the document allocates roughly six sections to instrument work and gives lever 1 three clauses in P3 — no files, no size, no owner, and gated behind P1. The plan reproduces the imbalance it names. If grok's top self-deception call is "mistaking the cleanup of the lab's conscience for progress on the product," then P3 should be Task 1 with real steps (building-skills iter4: which reference files, what char budget, what the reshape actually cuts), and the instrument items should be an appendix.

Related: the ADOPT track is the largest line item in the document — "~10pd" Inspect AI substrate swap, owner-endorsed — and it gets one parenthetical inside the status header. It needs its own plan, and it needs an answer to a consequence nobody wrote down: **does swapping substrate invalidate comparability of the existing benchmark dirs?** If prior KEEP/MERGE verdicts become historical-only, that changes what P1's re-measure ledger is even for.

## Specific defects

**Unmade decisions disguised as cheap fixes.** P0.6 "carry measured status or cut," P0.7 "relocate or cut," P0.8 "defer to the script" (how? is validate.py importable, or is this a generated-block-with-check?), P2b "Decide: rename vs disambiguation." Each is a fork an implementer will resolve by coin flip.

**Patching instances of a class instead of the class.** P0.4 (stale ADR 0065/0066/0076 cites), P0.5 (stale `benchmarks/lib/README.md` cite that 0089(b) missed), and P0.9 ("'3+ cases' floor stated in 4 files") are all the same bug: facts duplicated across files with nothing enforcing them. 0089(b) already missed a site once — hand-patching guarantees a third recurrence. The DRY fix is a test that walks every ADR reference and every duplicated constant against the retired-ids map and `validate.py`'s limits. That's a real task with a real failing test, and it's the highest-leverage item in P0.

**#303's evidence has no home.** You're closing an issue on a simulation that lives in "scratchpad coverage303.py" with the results table "in the session log." That's an unreproducible basis for a standing instrument decision. Promote the sim into the repo with a fixed seed and a test asserting the coverage bounds you're claiming, or the KEEP-t decision becomes folklore the moment the scratchpad is cleared.

**#317's recommendation contradicts its own finding.** You establish that n-grams *understate* the coupling and that the real DV contamination is house doctrine ("frontmatter order," "cut Background"). Then you adopt a per-benchmark **trigram overlap report** as the standing caveat. A report showing 1.4–3.6% will read as reassurance about a problem you just said it can't see. If doctrine is the DV, the caveat should say so in prose; the n-gram number is at best a footnote.

**Direct internal contradiction on pre-registration.** P3's stop-list: "pre-reg drafting without a spend decision." #302's recommendation (iii): a "NEW cheap pre-reg" for C5. Pick one. (I'd keep C5 — building-skills vs bare as a live loss condition is the most honest thing in the document — and amend the stop-list to exempt pre-regs that carry a spend decision and a decision rule. But then C5 needs its rule and its G stated up front, and per #303's own residual that means G≥8.)

**Two "standing caveat" artifacts.** P0.3 adds one to the README Measured block; #317 adds one per-benchmark. If those aren't the same artifact in one place, they will diverge — which is exactly the failure mode P0 exists to fix.

**The rename has zero file inventory.** It's confirmed, it's the highest blast radius item here (plugin id, marketplace entry, install paths, every cite, the retired-ids map, the org-collision rationale), and it has no file list and no verification step. If it "executes LAST, own PR," it is the one thing in this document that is fully specifiable *today* — so specify it.

## What I'd write next

Three documents, in this order: (1) the lever-1 plan (building-skills iter4 + optimizing-context re-measure) with real tasks; (2) the rename PR plan with a complete file inventory and a grep-based verification step; (3) the Inspect AI adoption plan with the comparability question answered and a kill criterion. Demote everything else to a status record.

One thing to keep as-is: bounding the #310 sweep at one consolidated round 2 and then writing the residual-risk ADR "regardless of quiet." That's the only place in the document where an open-ended loop gets a hard stop, and it's the right call.
